Looking at the sun can damage the eyes. Because its strong light falls on the delicate part at the back of the eye that senses light, and that part can be harmed even if it does not hurt at that moment, the eye should be protected.
Why do some people prefer a quiet evening at home to a big party?

People differ in how they get their energy. Because some people feel drained by crowds and noise, while others feel lively, a quiet evening can be restful for some people, while a party suits others better.
Why does a map have a key?

A map has a key to explain its symbols. Because the symbols are only drawings that stand for things like roads, rivers and schools, a reader who does not know the meaning would have to guess, and the key tells them.
Why does ironing make crumpled clothes smooth?

Ironing smooths clothes because heat and pressure reset the fibres. Because warmth makes the fibres soft and willing to move, and the weight of the iron presses them flat as they cool, the cloth keeps the smooth shape.
Why is it good to turn off the tap while brushing our teeth?
Turning off the tap saves water. Because running water keeps flowing whether we use it or not, closing the tap lets us use only what we need for rinsing.
Why does the sun seem to rise in the east?

The sun seems to rise in the east because the Earth turns toward the east. Because our own spot is carried around with the spinning Earth, we are turned toward the sun in the morning from that side, and it appears to climb into the sky.
Why do electricians use screwdrivers with plastic or rubber handles?
The handles protect the hand. Because rubber and plastic do not let electricity flow through them easily, a current in the metal cannot reach the person's hand, and the handle also gives a good grip.
Why does it hurt when friends plan an outing and do not invite us?
It hurts because we feel left out. Because people have a deep need to belong to a group, being left out feels like losing a place that matters to us, even when no harm was meant.
Why does food take longer to cook on a high mountain?
Food cooks more slowly on a mountain. Because the air pressure is lower there, water boils at a lower temperature, and water that is not as hot cooks the food more slowly.
Why do we remember embarrassing moments so clearly for years?

Embarrassing moments stay in memory because the feelings were strong. Because the brain stores events that stir powerful emotions more firmly than ordinary ones, and we replay them again in our minds, the memory stays sharp.
Why should an electric heater never be used to dry clothes by draping them over it?

Draping clothes over a heater is dangerous. Because cloth touching or close to a hot heater can heat up until it catches fire, and a covered heater also cannot let its own heat escape, it can overheat.
If a classmate stays silent when we greet them, does that prove they are being rude?
No, it does not prove that. Because many things can explain silence, such as shyness, worry, not hearing us or thinking about something else, it is fairer to ask kindly than to decide they are rude.
Why do birds fluff up their feathers on a cold morning?
Fluffed feathers keep a bird warmer. Because puffing them up traps more air close to the body, and still air is a poor carrier of heat, less warmth escapes from the bird.
Why do stars twinkle while planets shine steadily?

Stars twinkle because their light is shaken on its way to us. Because a star is so far away that it is a tiny point and the moving layers of our air shift that point about, while a planet is a larger disc and looks steadier, stars flicker and planets do not.
Why do group projects sometimes go wrong when nobody decides who does what?
Unclear roles make a group project go wrong. Because each person can assume that someone else is looking after a task, some jobs get done by many people and others by nobody.
Fish is to water as bird is to what?
The answer is air. Because a fish lives and moves in water, in the same way a bird lives and flies in the air.
Why does a woollen sweater shrink when it is washed in very hot water?

The sweater shrinks because the wool fibres tighten and tangle. Because the heat and the rubbing in the wash make the tiny scales on the fibres lock together, the cloth pulls in and cannot return to its old size.
A friend saw the cricket match herself. Another friend only heard about it from someone else. Whose account is likely to be more reliable?

The friend who saw it herself is likely to be more reliable. Because she watched the events directly, her account has not passed through anyone else, while a story heard second-hand can be changed or mixed up on the way.
Why should we leave home earlier than needed on the day of an exam?
Leaving early is sensible. Because buses can be late and roads can be blocked, extra time means that a delay does not make us miss the start of the exam.
Why does the smell of perfume seem to fade after a while even though it is still there?

The smell seems to fade because the nose gets used to it. Because the smell cells send weaker signals when they meet the same scent again and again, the brain stops noticing it, while someone who has just walked in still smells it.
Why do cracks appear in a muddy field in a long dry spell?
The cracks appear because the mud shrinks as it dries. Because the water leaving the soil makes it pull together, and the surface cannot shrink evenly, it splits into pieces.
Why do window panes rattle during a loud clap of thunder?
The panes rattle because sound can shake things. Because a loud sound is a series of strong pressure changes in the air, and the thin glass is pushed back and forth by them, it vibrates in its frame.
Why do the heels of shoes usually wear out first?

Heels wear out first because they take the hardest knock. Because the heel is the part that lands on the ground first and carries the weight of the body at every step, it rubs against the ground more than the rest of the sole.
Why is it sometimes hard to say no to a friend?
Saying no is hard because we fear letting the friend down. Because we value the friendship and worry that a refusal might upset them or spoil the bond, we may agree even when we do not want to.
Why do cooks keep stirring a pot of thick soup?
Stirring keeps the soup from burning. Because the bottom of the pot gets the most heat, soup that stays there can stick and scorch, and stirring moves it around and spreads the heat evenly.
Why should the handle of a pan on the stove be turned inward?
An inward handle is safer. Because a handle that sticks out can be knocked by a passing arm or a child's hand, and a knocked pan tips hot food onto people, keeping it inward lowers the risk.
Why does a rumour spread so fast?

A rumour spreads fast because people like to share surprising news. Because each person who hears it passes it on without checking whether it is true, and the story is often made more exciting on the way, it travels quickly.
Why is it wise to wait before replying to an angry message?
Waiting is wise because anger fades. Because strong anger makes us choose harsher words than we really mean, a short pause lets us calm down and write a reply that is less likely to hurt.
Why can we smell flowers more strongly on a warm morning than on a cold morning?
Flowers smell stronger in the warmth. Because heat helps the scent particles escape from the petals and drift through the air faster, more of them reach our noses.
Why do cows swish their tails again and again?
Cows swish their tails to chase away flies. Because flies land on the skin and bite or tickle, and the tail is the part that can reach most of the body, a swish drives them off.
Why is a car that has stood in the sun with its windows shut so hot inside?

The car gets hot because the heat is trapped. Because sunlight passes through the glass and warms the seats and the inside of the car, and the warmed things give off heat that cannot easily get back out through the glass, the air inside heats up.
Why does handwriting get messy when we write in a hurry?
Handwriting gets messy because speed leaves less control. Because the hand has less time to guide each stroke when it moves fast, the letters lose their shape and the lines wander.
Every time Uma washes her scooter, it rains. Does washing the scooter make it rain?
No, washing does not cause rain. Because things that happen together do not prove that the first causes the second, the rain comes from the weather, and the washing is just a coincidence.
Why is it useful to keep important papers in the same place at home?

Keeping papers together in a fixed place saves time. Because we will know where to look when we need them in a hurry, we do not waste time searching or risk losing a document that cannot be replaced easily.
Why does the water in a deep well stay cool even in the hot season?
The well water stays cool because it is deep under the ground. Because the heat of the sun hardly reaches far below the surface, the ground around the well stays cool all through summer.
Why does a bell go on ringing for a while after it has been struck?

The bell keeps ringing because the metal keeps shaking. Because the blow sets the whole metal body vibrating and the vibration only dies down slowly, the shaking air carries the sound to our ears for some time.
Why does a gift feel special when the giver remembered something we like?
Such a gift feels special because it shows that the giver paid attention to us. Because we can tell that they thought about us and not just about buying something, we feel noticed and cared for.
Why does an iron nail left out in the rain turn reddish-brown?
The nail is rusting. Because iron slowly joins with oxygen when water is present, it forms a reddish-brown flaky coating called rust.
Why do we feel chilly when we step out of a swimming pool, even on a warm day?
We feel chilly because the water on our skin is drying. Because water that turns to vapour takes heat from the skin as it leaves, the wet body loses warmth faster than a dry body.
Why can we shape wet sand into a castle but not dry sand?
Wet sand can hold a shape because the water holds the grains together. Because a thin film of water pulls neighbouring grains toward each other, they stick, while dry grains just slide apart.
Why can good friends disagree even when they like each other very much?

Friends can disagree because liking someone does not make people think alike. Because each person has different wishes and opinions, disagreements will happen, and talking about them calmly can even make a friendship stronger.
Why does ghee turn solid in the winter?
Ghee turns solid in the cold because its fats set. Because the fats stay liquid only when they are warm enough, and cooler air takes away their heat, they thicken and become firm.
Why does cooking oil start to smoke when it gets too hot?

Oil smokes because it begins to break down. Because heat beyond what the oil can stand splits its substances into vapours, smoke rises from the pan, and the oil can then catch fire, so the pan must be taken off the heat.
Why might children feel sad when their favourite teacher leaves the school?
The children feel sad because they have lost a person who mattered to them. Because they formed a bond with someone who encouraged them every day, they miss the support and the routine they shared.
Why does the sea rise and fall at the shore each day?

The sea rises and falls because of the pull of the moon. Because the moon's gravity tugs on the water of the oceans as the Earth turns, the water heaps up on some shores and draws back from others, and we see this as the tides.
Why is it kind to ask before taking someone's photograph?

Asking is kind because the picture is about the other person. Because everyone has a right to decide how their face is shared, and some people may not want to be photographed, a question shows respect.
Why do we feel awkward when we forget the name of someone we have met before?
We feel awkward because we worry about hurting the person. Because a name is part of how people feel known and remembered, forgetting it can seem like a sign that we did not care, even when we did.
Why can a parrot say words it has heard?

A parrot can copy words because it copies sounds. Because parrots are very good at imitating what they hear and often copy the voices of the people who live with them, they learn to repeat words without knowing what they mean.
Why does a fan make us feel cooler even though it does not cool the air?
A fan helps us feel cooler by helping sweat dry. Because moving air carries away the moisture on our skin and the drying takes heat from the body, we feel cooler even though the air is no colder.
If I stand facing north and turn to my right, which direction am I facing?
You would be facing east. Because east lies to the right of north when we go around the compass the way a clock's hands move, turning right from north brings us to the east.
Why does it help to read the whole question before starting to write an answer?

Reading the whole question helps us answer what is really asked. Because the last words often add a condition or a limit, a student who starts after reading only the first part may write a good answer to the wrong question.
Why is it a good habit to put things back where they belong?
Putting things back saves time. Because we will know where to look the next time we need them, and nobody else has to search either, little things do not get lost.
Why does smoke from a fire rise?
Smoke rises because the air around the fire is hot. Because hot air is lighter than the cooler air around it, it floats upward and carries the smoke with it.
Why is the ground cooler under a big tree in summer?

The ground is cooler because the tree makes shade. Because the leaves block much of the sunlight and the tree also gives off water vapour from its leaves, which cools the air around them, the spot stays pleasant.
Why do old photographs fade when they are left in the sunlight?
Photographs fade because light breaks down their colours. Because the energy in sunlight slowly damages the dyes that make the picture, the colours become paler year after year.
Why does a baby smile back when we smile at it?

A baby smiles back because it responds to friendly faces. Because babies learn about the world by watching the faces of people around them and a smile signals safety and warmth, they soon answer it in the same way.
Why does an empty room echo more than a room full of furniture?

An empty room echoes more because its bare walls and floor bounce sound back. Because curtains, sofas and rugs are soft and soak up part of the sound, a furnished room sends much less of it back to our ears.
Why do we trust a friend who has always kept their promises?

We trust such a friend because past behaviour is the best clue we have. Because a person who has kept their word many times has shown that they care about doing so, we expect them to do the same again.
Why do young children enjoy pretend games such as playing shop or doctor?
Pretend play helps children learn about the world. Because they can try out roles, talk the way grown-ups do and practise solving little problems in a safe way, they understand how people behave.
Why does milk suddenly rush over the rim of the pot when it boils?
The milk rises because a skin forms on top. Because the skin traps the steam bubbles that are rising from below, the bubbles lift the whole layer up and over the edge in a moment.
Why do many birds sing loudly at dawn?
Birds sing at dawn because it is a good time to be heard. Because the air is calm in the early morning and the sound carries far, birds call to mark their territory and to attract mates.
Why should we not feed wild monkeys?
Feeding wild monkeys is a bad idea. Because they soon learn to link people with food and lose their fear, they may grab bags and snatch food, and sometimes they bite.
Why do we often feel nervous just before we speak in front of the whole class?

Nervousness is natural before speaking to a crowd. Because the body treats the moment as a challenge and releases stress hormones that make the heart race and the hands shake, and because we care what others will think of us, the feeling is strong.
Why do owls hunt at night while sparrows sleep?

Owls hunt at night because their bodies suit the dark. Because their big eyes gather dim light and their hearing is very sharp, they can find mice and insects at night when most other birds are asleep.
Why do we squint when the sun is very bright?
Squinting cuts down the glare. Because narrowing the eyelids lets less light into the eye, it helps us see in strong light and protects the eye a little.
Why is a person who admits a mistake often easier to trust?
Admitting a mistake builds trust. Because it shows that the person is honest even when it is uncomfortable, we can believe that they will tell us the truth in future as well.
Why is it rude to interrupt someone who is speaking?

Interrupting is rude because it shows we do not value what the speaker is saying. Because the speaker also loses their train of thought and may not get to finish, the talk becomes frustrating for them.
Why should a seed be planted in damp soil and not left on a dry shelf?
A seed sprouts only when it gets water. Because water soaks into the seed and wakes up the tiny plant inside, damp soil lets it start growing, while a dry shelf keeps it sleeping.
Ravi says that every dog on his street barks. Pepper is a dog on his street and she never barks. Is Ravi right?
No, Ravi is not right. Because a dog that never barks is enough to show that not every dog barks, his statement is false.
Why does a bicycle speed up when it rolls down a slope without pedalling?
The bicycle speeds up because gravity pulls it downhill. Because gravity keeps adding a push in the direction of the slope, and little friction works against it, the bicycle gains speed.
How does a daily timetable work better with gaps left for rest?
Gaps for rest make a timetable work. Because tasks often take longer than expected and a tired mind works badly, a short break keeps delays from piling up and helps us do better work.
Why does a whiteboard marker dry out if the cap is left off?
The marker dries out because the liquid in it evaporates. Because the ink contains a liquid that turns into vapour in open air, it escapes from the tip, and what is left is too dry to write.
Why do all the players of a team wear shirts of the same colour?
Matching shirts help everybody tell who plays for which side. Because players, umpires and the crowd can then see at a glance who is a teammate and who is an opponent, the game is easier to follow.
Why does the smell of cooking spread right through the house?

Smells spread because tiny particles of food drift through the air. Because the particles move about on their own and are carried along by every small current in the room, they reach other rooms and our noses.
Why does a crying baby often calm down when it is picked up and held?
A held baby feels safer. Because being close to a caring person's warmth and heartbeat tells the baby it is not alone, and being picked up shows that its cry was heard, the baby relaxes.
Why does a kind word from a friend lift our mood?
A kind word lifts our mood because it makes us feel valued. Because people need to feel that others accept them, hearing a warm remark eases worry and brings the pleasant feeling of belonging.
Why does a paper boat sink after floating for a while?
The paper boat sinks because it soaks up water. Because wet paper becomes heavy and loses its stiffness, the sides sag, and water flows in over the edge.
Why can we sometimes see the moon in the daytime?

We can see the moon in the daytime because it is sometimes above the horizon while the sun is too. Because the moon travels around the Earth and rises at different hours from day to day, and sunlight on its surface is bright enough to see, it can show up against the blue sky.
Why does a team usually do better when its members listen to each other?
A team does better when everyone listens. Because ideas are shared, mistakes are noticed early and nobody works against the others by accident, the team uses all its members' knowledge.
Why should a child ask an adult before taking any medicine?

Asking an adult is safer. Because the wrong medicine, or the wrong amount, can harm a child, and an adult can read the label and check with a doctor or pharmacist, the choice is made with proper knowledge.
Why does blowing across the top of an empty bottle make a humming sound?

The hum comes from the air inside the bottle. Because the stream of air across the opening makes the air in the bottle vibrate, and the size of the bottle decides which note is loudest, we hear a steady tone.
Why does a spinning coin finally fall flat on the table?
The coin falls because it slowly loses its spin. Because friction with the table and the air takes away the energy of the spin, it can no longer stay upright, and it wobbles and drops.
Why does a tiger have stripes?
The stripes help a tiger hide. Because the dark stripes break up the outline of its body among tall grass and the shadows of leaves, its prey finds it hard to see until it is close.
Why do our cheeks turn red when we are embarrassed?
Our cheeks turn red because more blood flows to the skin of the face. Because a rush of strong feeling makes the tiny blood vessels there widen, the skin shows the colour of the blood.
Why do shadows grow long in the late afternoon?

Shadows grow long because the sun is low. Because light from a low sun reaches objects at a slant, it throws their shadows far across the ground, while from high overhead it falls almost straight down and the shadow stays short.
Why might a person refuse help even when they really need it?
A person may refuse help because of pride or worry. Because they may not want to seem weak or may feel that they are a burden to others, they say no, even when help would make things easier.
Why do flower pots need small holes at the bottom?
The holes let extra water drain out. Because roots need air as well as water, and soil that stays soggy leaves no room for air, roots in a pot without holes can start to rot.
If the bell rings, school ends. School has not ended yet. Has the bell rung?
No, the bell has not rung. Because school would have ended if the bell had rung, and it has not ended, the bell cannot have rung yet.
Why do people wear layers of clothes on a mountain walk?
Layers work better than a thick garment. Because the weather and our own body heat change during the walk, we can take off a layer when we are warm and put it on again when the wind turns cold.
Why does a hot road seem to shine like water far ahead in the afternoon?

The shine is a trick of light, not real water. Because the air touching the hot road is much hotter than the air above it and bends light coming down from the sky back up to our eyes, we see a patch of sky that looks like a puddle.
Why is it good manners to say thank you when someone helps us?
Saying thank you is good manners because it shows we noticed the help. Because people like to know that their effort mattered, thanks makes them feel respected and more willing to help again.
Why does a hot pan sizzle when a drop of water falls onto it?

The drop sizzles because it turns to steam almost instantly. Because the metal is far hotter than the water's boiling point, the water boils away in an instant, and the bursting bubbles make the noise.
Why do exam halls have a clock on the wall?
The clock lets students watch the time for themselves. Because they can see how much time is left without interrupting anyone, they can plan how long to spend on each question.
Why does telling an angry person to calm down often make them angrier?
The remark often makes anger worse. Because those words can sound as if the person's feelings do not matter, they feel unheard and more upset, while listening first helps the feeling to ease.
Why does a plant on a sunny window sill dry out faster than a plant in a shady corner?
The window plant dries out faster because the sun heats it. Because warmth and moving air carry water out of the soil and the leaves more quickly, the plant in sunshine needs water sooner.
